patch.objective: Build and prioritize a differential diagnosis from history, examination and test results, ruling out the dangerous causes first
secondaryObjectives: Select the diagnostic test that will change management, and interpret its result

sources.cite: Jaqua EE, Nguyen VTN, Chin E. Delirium in older persons: prevention, evaluation, and management. Am Fam Physician 2023;108(3):278-287
sources.note: Relayed from the FNP clinical case two-falls-not-herself, not re-read for this band; its note: Read 2026-11-17 through a summarizing fetch with quotes. Delirium is an 'acute disturbance in attention, cognition, and awareness that fluctuates over time' that 'develops over a short period of time'; it 'can be precipitated by medications, adverse medication effects, uncontrolled pain, infections', and urinary or stool retention.

sources.cite: Washington State Department of Health. Medical Providers' Frequently Asked Questions About Urinary Tract Infections (DOH 420-466, March 2023)
sources.note: Relayed from the FNP clinical case two-falls-not-herself, not re-read for this band; its note: Read 2026-11-17 through a summarizing fetch with quotes. The IDSA 2019 guideline makes a 'strong recommendation against treating ASB' in older adults; patients who 'are delirious but have no UTI symptoms or systemic signs of infections' should be evaluated for other causes ('IDSA recommends investigating first for other causes for delirium'); 'Falls are, therefore, not considered to be associated with UTI in the elderly'; 'a positive UA on its own is not a very reliable indicator of UTI'.
